episodes.title: The Sussex Village Hiding A Cult, A Queen, And A Font And I Go Looking For Jacobs Post
episodes.description:
In this episode of Doorstep Explorer, we're in the shadow of the highest point on the South Downs, in a village that's been a Saxon stronghold, a queen's bolt-hole, and the unlikely capital of English lettering.

It starts with the Saxons, and a Norman church that's been quietly watching the village change around it ever since. From there it's on to Wings Place, where Anne of Cleves landed part of her divorce settlement from Henry VIII and, by most accounts, considerably improved her situation by not being married to him.

Then things get strange in a very Ditchling way: Eric Gill arrived in the 1920s and built a community of artists and stonemasons calling itself the Guild of St Joseph and St Dominic — part religious order, part arts colony. His neighbour Edward Johnston, meanwhile, was quietly designing the typeface that still tells half of London which platform to stand on.

We climb Ditchling Beacon for the view, then go hunting along the ridge for Jacob's Post — the old gibbet site with a name that's outlasted the story behind it, and a spot that takes a bit more finding than the map suggests.

We finish, as ever, with a pint at The Bull.
